# KL3001 `missing-memory-limit`

A container has no `resources.limits.memory`.

Category: `reliability`. Severity: `warning`. Enabled by default.

## What it does

Reports a container in `containers` or `initContainers` without
`resources.limits.memory`, either because `resources`, `limits` or `memory` is missing,
or because one of them is null. Ephemeral containers are skipped, because Kubernetes
does not allow `resources` on them. A pod that sets its own `spec.resources.limits.memory`
(pod-level resources) bounds all its containers, so they are not reported.

## Why it matters

Without a memory limit, a container can use all the free memory of its node. A leak or
a traffic spike in one container then makes the node run out of memory, and the kernel
kills processes of other pods too, often ones that did nothing wrong. With a limit, only
the container that goes over it is restarted (`OOMKilled`), and the scheduler can place
pods knowing how much memory they may use at most. Some namespaces set a default limit
with a `LimitRange`, but the manifest cannot rely on it being there.

## Example

```yaml
containers:
- name: web
  image: nginx:1.27
  resources:
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
```

Use instead:

```yaml
containers:
- name: web
  image: nginx:1.27
  resources:
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
```
